lede: The one sector whose table cannot fill the map: it asks for at most 20 slots against a 24-beacon ceiling, so nothing on it is ever cut and the spare beacons draw from the galaxy-wide fallback list instead. What it does place is supply and repetition — three repair stations, one store, and the same Rebel scout on all six hostile beacons. The fight you came for is on none of those rows: the **Rebel Flagship** and the Federation Base are put on the map by the endgame.
callout: **Order does not matter here — and that is unique.** In every other sector the sequence of these rows decides what gets dropped once the map is full. This allocation tops out below the ceiling, so every row is placed in full every run and nothing is ever at risk. The overflow runs the other way instead: on a full map at least four beacons are left with nothing assigned, and they fall to the shared `NEUTRAL` fallback — ordinary galaxy events, no `BOSS_` prefix, none of them in the table below. **Pirate briber** is one that can turn up, which is also the only way this sector produces a second store.

section_notes.BOSS_HOSTILE: One event, written into the list three times, filling six beacons — every hostile beacon in the sector is the same encounter. Its ship is drawn from a roster of two crewed Rebel hulls and two automated ones, and it has no surrender branch and no escape branch: once {{BOSS_SCOUT}} starts, it runs to a wreck.
section_notes.BOSS_NEUTRAL: The only entry with any range in it, and the sector's entry beacon draws from here too. Not to be confused with the shared `NEUTRAL` list that fills the leftover beacons — same word, different list, no events in common. {{BOSS_FLEETS_BOTH_FIGHT}} and {{REBEL}} are fighting the moment you drop in; {{BOSS_FLEETS_FED}} is pure scenery; {{BOSS_SCOUT_RESCUE}} and {{SQUAT_REFUEL_STATION}} both let you decline.
section_notes.BOSS_REPAIR_STATION: No choices, no risk and no fight: 15 hull, every damaged system restored, 4 missiles, 5 fuel, 5 drone parts and 22–44 scrap, three times over. Each one is single-use, and each carries its own label on the map — so the supply here is the part you can see coming, and the part the fleet can take off the board before you reach it.
section_notes.STORE: One store, guaranteed, and the only beacon in the sector where scrap turns into anything. Nothing in this pool can open a second one.

chain.title: The Rebel Flagship · fought in three phases

steps.title: Arrive at the Federation Base
steps.detail: The entry event runs once and pays **10 fuel** and **10 hull repaired** before you jump anywhere. The base beacon itself is flavour: you hang back near the far side of the moon while the two fleets skirmish, and prepare to face the Flagship.

steps.title: Phase 1 — four artillery mounts
steps.detail: It carries no weapons and no drones; everything it fires comes from four artillery mounts, behind cloaking and four layers of shields. Advanced Edition adds a **Hacking** system and removes the Easy-difficulty shield discount.

steps.title: Phase 2 — the drone surge
steps.detail: One artillery mount fewer, and the drone system running at power 8. The only edition difference is the lost Easy-mode shield discount; the systems are otherwise identical between vanilla and Advanced Edition.

steps.title: Phase 3 — boarders and the super weapon
steps.detail: Two artillery mounts, engines at 6, a teleporter and an `invasion` boarding AI. Advanced Edition adds **Mind Control** — so in AE the last phase mind-controls your crew while it boards you, where vanilla only boards.

steps.title: It dies, or it jumps
steps.detail: A phase that loses its crew but keeps shooting is the AI taking over. A phase that breaks off pays a high standard reward and sends you after it. The kill event still ends on a leftover beta message thanking you for playing.

items.text: {{BOSS_REPAIR_STATION}} is a fixed three beacons: 15 hull, every damaged system restored, 4 missiles, 5 fuel, 5 drone parts and 22–44 scrap, each time.
Entering the sector pays 10 fuel and repairs 10 hull before you have jumped anywhere.
{{BOSS_SCOUT_RESCUE}} can repair 8 more hull — one of three outcomes after you save the cruiser, the others being thanks and a bundle of supplies.
{{SQUAT_REFUEL_STATION}} pays a fuel bonus from the grateful outpost on top of the salvage, but only if you choose to intervene.
Two events can hand you a crew member, {{BOSS_SCOUT}} and {{REBEL}}, and only through the dead-crew salvage — the prisoner is found aboard a ship whose crew you killed, not one you blew up.
Exactly one, allocated 1–1, and the last place to spend scrap before the Flagship.
This is the only sector with no exit beacon at all, so the shared exit list that fills one everywhere else never runs. Nothing on this map is a way out.

Nothing in the pool carries the distress tag and no distress line is allocated, so that marker never appears here. The only thing the map labels ahead of time is supply: the store, and the three repair stations.

Toward the middle-right of the grid, and the game places it a fixed distance from your arrival — four jumps away on easy and normal, five to six on hard. The Flagship spawns in the two right-most columns, four to six jumps from the base.
The fleet does not sweep in from the left here. It takes scattered individual beacons each turn, and the Flagship takes whatever it is sitting on — so danger arrives behind you as readily as ahead.
You can hold at a beacon with fuel still in the tank. It ticks the map forward like a jump, and a fight that starts after a wait begins with your FTL already charged.
{{BOSS_SCOUT}} fills every hostile beacon, and the ship it loads has no surrender and no escape branch. Every one of the six ends in a destroyed hull or a dead crew.

A beacon the fleet takes loses whatever was on it — including a repair station you were saving — and becomes an Elite Fighter under an anti-ship battery, paying one fuel for the kill. There is nothing to farm there.
{{BOSS_FLEETS_BOTH_FIGHT}} is fighting on arrival and pays a low, scrap-only reward when destroyed — the text says outright there is no time to salvage the wreck.
{{REBEL}} can surrender or power up its FTL and leave, so a beacon that looks like scrap can end with neither the fight nor the salvage.
No event in this pool puts boarders aboard and none can kill a crew member. What the sector takes is hull and ammunition, across the six guaranteed fights plus whatever the neutral pool adds.
None. Not one event in the pool has a gated choice, so no system level, augment or crew species changes a single outcome in this sector.

No quest line is allocated and nothing in the pool plants a marker — this sector cannot hold a quest at all. A quest you trigger in the sector before it is not carried forward either; it is simply dropped.
Nothing here unlocks a ship or hands out a named weapon or augment.
No event in the pool names a crew type, and the sector declares no rarity list of its own — nothing in this sector's data tunes what the store's crew slots offer.
{{SQUAT_REFUEL_STATION}} is the only event here carrying the files' own unique flag.
